initial_description:
Okay, I will generate a detailed description of the illustrative figure based on your provided methodology section and figure caption.

**Overall Layout:**

The figure is a panoramic banner (2400x700 pixels) with a left-to-right flow. It is divided into three main sections: Command Input (left, gray), Geofence (center, orange/amber), and Spatial Result (right). The overall goal is to visualize how the Probabilistic Dynamic Geofence protects a robot from entering forbidden zones. All elements are designed to be compact and horizontally aligned, minimizing vertical space.

**Left Section (Command Input - Gray, narrow, ~20% of width):**

*   A user icon (a generic silhouette of a person) is located on the far left. It uses a muted gray color to indicate that this is an untrusted input.
*   An arrow (medium gray, thin line, closed arrowhead) points from the user icon to a rectangular box labeled "LLM Planner". The box has a light gray fill and a thin gray border.
*   Another arrow (medium gray, thin line, closed arrowhead) points from the "LLM Planner" box to a rectangular box labeled "Nav2". This box also has a light gray fill and a thin gray border.
*   All three elements (user icon, LLM Planner box, and Nav2 box) are horizontally aligned.

**Center Section (Geofence - Orange Border, Light Amber Background, ~45% of width):**

*   This section has a light amber background fill and a prominent orange border. It is divided into two halves, side by side.
*   **Left Half: Goal Gate (Before robot moves)**
    *   A decision diamond labeled "Safe?" is at the top. The diamond has a thin black border and a white fill.
    *   An arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) points from the top point of the diamond DOWN.
    *   If the answer to "Safe?" is NO, an arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) branches to the left to a rectangular box labeled "BLOCK" with a red fill and thin black border.
    *   If the answer to "Safe?" is NO, another arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) branches to the right to a rectangular box labeled "PROJECT" with an orange fill and thin black border.
    *   If the answer to "Safe?" is YES, an arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) points straight to the next stage (Cmd Vel Guard). The arrow is labeled "Allow" in small text.
    *   Small label below the Goal Gate: "Before robot moves".
*   **Right Half: Cmd Vel Guard (During motion)**
    *   A decision diamond labeled "Safe?" is at the top. The diamond has a thin black border and a white fill.
    *   An arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) points from the top point of the diamond DOWN.
    *   If the answer to "Safe?" is NO, an arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) points to a rectangular box labeled "STOP" with a red fill and thin black border.
    *   If the answer to "Safe?" is YES, a loop arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) indicates continuous monitoring. This loop arrow curves back to the input of the "Safe?" diamond.
    *   Small label below the Cmd Vel Guard: "During motion".
*   A label "Dynamic Safety Margin M(t)" is placed at the bottom center of the entire Geofence section, in small text.

**Right Section (Spatial Result - Bird's-Eye View, ~35% of width):**

*   This section depicts a top-down spatial view.
*   A red rectangle represents the "Forbidden Zone".
*   A dashed orange border surrounds the red rectangle, representing "M(t)" (the dynamic safety margin).
*   A dashed arrow (thin black line, closed arrowhead) originates from the left side of the section (representing the intended path). This arrow is interrupted by a large red "X" symbol at the orange border (M(t)).
*   A small robot icon (a simplified robot shape, not a circle, colored blue) is positioned at the point where the dashed arrow is interrupted, just outside the red "Forbidden Zone" and touching the orange dashed border.
*   The text "Blocked!" is displayed in red near the robot icon.

**Styling:**

*   The background is pure white.
*   The color palette is: Orange (geofence), Gray (untrusted input), Red (danger/blocked), Blue (robot).
*   Lines are thin (1-2 pixels).
*   Arrows have closed arrowheads.
*   No gradients, 3D effects, or shadows.
*   Text is small and concise.
*   The overall style is clean and academic, suitable for an IEEE paper.
*   Font is a standard sans-serif font (e.g., Arial, Helvetica).
